key_insight: Introduce a learned latent-dynamics representation that encodes motion history and hidden state (inertia, contact) so a pose-conditioned neural renderer can produce realistic, history-dependent deformations (e.g., loose clothing) without per-garment templates.
problem_solved: Pose-only avatar models cannot capture history-dependent deformations (the same pose can map to many clothing states); explicit simulation or garment templates are costly or unavailable for raw multi-view capture pipelines.
method: Learn a compact latent state that summarizes recent motion, contact and inertia from raw multi-view capture sequences.
Train a temporal dynamics model that updates the latent state conditioned on incoming poses/motion so the current deformation reflects history.
Condition a neural rendering pipeline on both the current pose and the latent state to synthesize novel-view, full-body animations without dedicated garment templates.
impact: Enables more realistic, physically plausible full-body avatars from routine multi-view captures while removing the need for manual garment templates or expensive simulations — useful for telepresence, VFX, gaming, and dataset-efficient avatar creation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-view capture → latent dynamics module (time series icon) → pose+latent → neural renderer → novel view outputs.
Before/after comparison: pose-only rendering vs. latent-dynamics rendering showing improved cloth folds and motion realism.
Latent trajectory plot: short timeline visualizing how the latent state evolves for the same target pose under different motion histories.
Icon set: camera array (capture), clock/inertia (history), neural net (renderer), and a crossed-out garment-template icon to emphasize template-free operation.
paper_title: Latent Dynamics for Full Body Avatar Animation
paper_authors: Shichong Peng, Chengxiang Yin, Fei Jiang, Zhongshi Jiang, Lingchen Yang
